vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: sql-generator
Version: 2.3.3

The SQL Generator skill is a legitimate utility designed to generate SQL templates (DDL, queries, and mock data) based on user input. The core logic in `scripts/sql.sh` uses standard shell commands to output predefined text blocks and does not perform any network requests, sensitive file access, or command execution on the host system.

llm.summary: The skill appears to implement an on-disk Bash SQL generator and helper (DDL, mock data, explain, etc.) that matches its description and does not request credentials or install remote components.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (SQL generator, DDL creator, mock data, migration, cheatsheet) align with the included SKILL.md, tips.md, and scripts/sql.sh which generate SQL DDL and examples. There are no unrelated required binaries, env vars, or config paths.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs use of the provided script and lists SQL-related commands; the script's visible portions generate SQL and print example DDL. The instructions do not ask the agent to read unrelated system files or exfiltrate data. Note: a portion of scripts/sql.sh in the provided bundle was truncated in the listing — the assessment is based on the visible content.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only plus an included shell script). That is low-risk compared to downloads/third-party package installs; the bundle writes no external installers or fetchers.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials and the visible script does not reference secrets or remote API keys.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false, user-invocable is true, and the skill does not request persistent system privileges or modify other skills' config in the visible files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and self-contained, but before installing: (1) inspect the full scripts/sql.sh (the listing was truncated here) to ensure no hidden network requests, curl/wget calls, or exec of untrusted commands; (2) run it in a sandbox or container first (don't run as root); (3) verify the publisher/source (no homepage provided) and license if you will use it in production; (4) if you plan to connect it to real databases, ensure credentials are provided only at runtime and not baked into the script. If you find any network calls or references to external endpoints in the truncated portion, treat that as a red flag and re-evaluate.
